title: Failure Mode: False-Positive Explosion in Behavioral Anomaly Detectors for Agents

original_idea.body:
# Failure Mode: False-Positive Explosion in Behavioral Anomaly Detectors for Agents

**Problem:** Any anomaly-based detection system for agentic behavior risks high false-positive rates as legitimate agents perform unusual-but-benign actions. This failure mode can render anomaly detectors operationally useless via alert fatigue.

**Direction:** Implement a behavioral anomaly detector for agent action streams. Run it on a diverse set of 100 benign agentic tasks (with legitimate variability). Measure false-positive rate across task diversity levels. Identify which task types produce the most false positives and why.

**Why it matters:** High false-positive rates are a known operational failure mode in IDS systems, leading to detector abandonment. Characterizing this failure mode for agentic anomaly detection is a prerequisite for practical deployment.

**Relevant context:** IDS false-positive problem; alert fatigue in security operations; anomaly detection literature; METR 2026 monitoring.
